abstinence

AB-stih-nents -- stress on the first syllable, AB. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Abstinence is self-restraint from an indulgence; the practice of going without something.

Her month of abstinence from social media left her calmer, better rested, and surprised by how much free time she had.

Example

For the forty days before the festival, the villagers practice complete abstinence from sweets, not touching so much as a spoonful of sugar.

That sustained, deliberate practice of going without an indulgence is abstinence. It is not a single moment of saying no -- it is the ongoing state of self-denial, kept up day after day.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

temperance: Temperance is a principle of disciplined moderation — often enjoying a little and deliberately stopping there, and historically the virtue of avoiding alcohol. Abstinence is narrower and more absolute: the actual practice of going without an indulgence entirely, whether or not you hold it up as a virtue.

forbearance: Forbearance is patient self-control in the face of provocation — holding back a sharp reply or bearing an annoyance without complaint. Abstinence is about pleasures rather than reactions: the ongoing practice of going without an indulgence such as sweets, screens, or late nights.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

indulgence: the act of giving in to a desire or pleasure

excess: too much of something; overindulgence

Where it sits · how completely the indulgence is given up — self-restraint → abstinence → renunciation

self-restraint vs. abstinence: Self-restraint is broader and milder than abstinence -- it can mean holding back just a little or just once, while abstinence means going without the thing completely, usually over a sustained period.

renunciation vs. abstinence: Renunciation is more sweeping and more final than abstinence: abstinence gives up one indulgence, often for a set time, while renunciation gives something up formally and for good, the way a monk renounces worldly comforts forever.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — abs-

prefix — abs-: away, away from (Latin)

root — tin

root — tin: to hold (from Latin tenere; the same root appears as -tain in contain and retain)

suffix — -ence

suffix — -ence: state or quality of (Latin -entia)

Put it together

Put it together: Abstinence combines Latin abs- ('away from'), tenere ('to hold') -- here spelled -tin- -- and -ence ('the state of'). It is literally 'the state of holding oneself away' -- the ongoing condition of keeping your distance from an indulgence.

Use the root in a new word: contain

Use the root in a new word: contain: The firefighters worked through the night to contain the blaze before it reached the town.

Root Check

Word Choice

Abstinence is the noun in the word family whose verb is abstain: the verb names the act of holding back, while abstinence names the ongoing practice or state. It usually takes 'from' -- 'abstinence from sugar' -- and keeping it up for weeks takes genuine determination.
